chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace:
That a man came to Ali (peace be upon him) and said: 'I have a debt due from a man, and he gave me a gift.' He said: 'Count it as part of your debt.'
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic jurisprudence treat gifts given to settle or offset a debt?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the legal principle of *hiساب* (accounting) where a gift is treated as a voluntary debt settlement. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding debt resolution, emphasizing that unless explicitly restricted, a creditor may accept a gift as full or partial satisfaction of the owed amount, reflecting the spirit of ease in financial transactions.
